sources.title: Brief Review of Major Depressive Disorder for Primary Care Providers
sources.locator: Diagnosis section: depressed mood or anhedonia as the necessary element plus three to four associated criteria (poor energy, insomnia or hypersomnia, difficulty concentrating, guilt or worthlessness, psychomotor agitation or retardation, weight change of about 5%, thoughts of death), present most days over the previous two weeks; morbidity section on dysfunction across work, home life, self-care and adherence; assessment of past manic or hypomanic episodes

No wording, table, case, figure, or section order was copied or adapted; the elements are restated in this lesson's own language and applied to an invented case.

sources.title: Bipolar disorder
sources.locator: Clinical features: a distinct period of elevated, expansive or irritable mood with increased activity or energy, plus reduced need for sleep, pressured speech, flight of ideas, distractibility, grandiosity, impulsivity, and activities carrying high potential for painful consequences; seven-day and four-day duration thresholds for mania and hypomania; psychotic features in mania only; anxiety, agitation and irritability in mixed states; diagnostic delay and corroborative history
sources.license: No Creative Commons licence displayed on the checked PMC record; publisher copyright applies; citation-only factual reference

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Only bounded facts about the descriptive features of raised-activity periods, the conventional duration thresholds, the presence of anxiety, agitation and irritability in mixed states, the diagnostic delay, and the value of corroborative history were used. No sentence, table, figure, box, or organising structure from the seminar was copied or adapted.

sources.title: The prevalence and diagnostic classification of mixed features in patients with major depressive episodes: A multicenter study based on the DSM-5
sources.version: International Journal of Methods in Psychiatric Research 28(3):e1773; doi 10.1002/mpr.1773
sources.locator: Results: among 672 non-psychotic major depressive episodes drawn from 859 patients hospitalised across twelve centres in the Republic of Korea between October 2013 and September 2016, 5.8% met the DSM-5 mixed-features specifier and 31.7% met broader research-based diagnostic criteria; irritable mood was the commonest elevated feature at 90.8% among the 213 broader-criteria cases; discussion of reclassification as anxious distress or a cluster-B personality disorder
sources.license: © 2019 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.; no open licence displayed on the checked PMC record; citation-only factual reference

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Only the two prevalence figures on the same non-psychotic denominator, the commonest elevated feature and its frequency, and the finding about reclassification were used. No table, figure, sentence, or analytic structure from the paper was reproduced, and the figures are recontextualised to make a point about criterion dependence rather than to report the study.

sources.title: Challenges in the Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder With Psychotic Features
sources.publisher: Oxford University Press on behalf of the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center
sources.locator: Epidemiology and diagnosis sections: 14.7% of people meeting criteria for major depression in the United States Epidemiologic Catchment Area study had a history of psychotic features; 18.5% in a European sample; about 25% of hospitalised depressed patients; nihilistic delusional content; DSM-5 precedence for mood-incongruent features; 27% of 130 diagnoses in a well-characterised psychotic-depression sample initially incorrect, with the psychosis rather than the mood disorder missed

sources.title: Clinical practice guidelines on the assessment and management of cognitive impairment in major depressive disorder
sources.publisher: Wolters Kluwer — Medknow, for the Indian Journal of Psychiatry
sources.version: Indian Journal of Psychiatry 67(1):98–105; doi 10.4103/indianjpsychiatry.indianjpsychiatry_563_24; PMID 40046482
sources.locator: Cognitive domains affected in major depressive disorder (attention, memory and learning including semantic, episodic and working memory, executive function, psychomotor processing); statement that residual cognitive symptoms continue after resolution of an episode with persistent deficits at long-term follow-up; statement that cognitive deficits significantly affect occupational and social functioning

sources.title: Low self-recognition and awareness of past hypomanic and manic episodes in the general population
sources.version: International Journal of Bipolar Disorders 3:22; doi 10.1186/s40345-015-0039-8
sources.locator: Results: of 40 respondents aged 18–64 with structured-interview-confirmed lifetime DSM-IV bipolar disorder, drawn from the Netherlands Mental Health Survey and Incidence Study and reappraised in 2001–2002, 82.5% recognised a past depressive episode and 22.5% a past hypomanic or manic one; 75.0% had consulted a professional for depression and 17.5% for (hypo)mania; the 31 non-recognisers explained the periods as pleasant and productive, as part of their personality, or as circumstantial
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0); © Regeer et al. 2015

sources.title: Validity of retrospectively-reported depressive episodes
sources.version: Journal of Affective Disorders 277:908–913; doi 10.1016/j.jad.2020.08.067; PMID 33065833; PMC author manuscript
sources.locator: Results: 68 participants from the Oregon Adolescent Depression Project contributed 110 concurrent symptom mailers falling inside later retrospectively-reported depressive episodes and 135 falling between them; symptom scores were higher inside the reported episodes with a medium-to-large effect (d = .66); 54 of the 110 within-episode mailers (49.1%) reached the depression scale's clinical cut-off; length of the recall interval did not significantly moderate the association
sources.license: PMC author manuscript of an accepted article; no Creative Commons licence displayed; citation-only factual reference

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Only the design in outline, the direction and magnitude of the effect, the 49.1% cut-off figure, and the authors' conclusion about validity were used. No wording, table, figure, or instrument item from the paper was reproduced, and the finding is applied to an invented case.
